title: Dayap Cashew: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Dayap Cashew: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Dayap cashew is a cashew variety from Alvino Dayap. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Dayap is a registered cashew variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Cs 02. Alvino Dayap bred it. Its record notes a yield of 1,500 to 2,00 fruits.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Dayap cashew is grown

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 1,500 to 2,00 fruits.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Dayap was about 45 years old and about 15 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 1,500 to 2,00 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in March May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cashew fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its sweetness measured 15.1 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 35 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is March May, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Dayap cashew

Kasoy stands drought and poor soil, which is why Palawan grows so much of it. Pick a selection by nut weight and shelling recovery, which decide the kernel you sell. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Dayap?
